speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Firebird is another provider that debuted this summer at GTC Paris, backed by $500M from the Aermenian government with intention to buy GB300 NVL72 rack scale systems and a focus on sovereign AI.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: They have support from Telecom Armenia and Ireland’s Imagine Broadband.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Though a public offering is not yet launched, we are excited to test it in the future.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Firmus / Sustainable Metal Cloud (SMC) earns a ClusterMAX 2.0 Silver rating from SemiAnalysis.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Firmus is an Australian company that was recently backed by a strategic investment from Nvidia at a $1.9B valuation

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Their current ambition is to build a “Stargate for the southern hemisphere,” with a specific focus on next-generation rack-scale systems like the GB300 NVL72 and VR.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Though we believe that the bulk of Firmus’s experience with immersion cooling is misguided, and now wasted, we also believe that this team is one of the few in the industry that has the engineering chops to monitor and maintain the physical layer of these DLC systems effectively.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Our review of their current telemetry and failure prediction system for their immersion deployments demonstrates significant attention to detail, and a deep understanding of the physical stack, down to the signal quality and light levels in custom transceivers and optical cables.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: However, this experience at the lowest physical level can be undermined by a higher UX level that feels out-of-touch with customer requirements.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Our testing began with a difficult wrinkle: cluster access is gated behind a mandatory VPN.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: This is a significant operational bottleneck for teams accustomed to standard cloud workflows with public IPs or streamlined SSH wrappers.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: The fact that Firmus had no alternative access method prepared was telling for us.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Once connected, our slurm environment also had some configuration issues. The standard topology.conf file was not set for topology-aware scheduling, and a simple “srun -N1 –gpus-per-node=8 –pty bash” command took over a minute to execute due to an exceptionally long prolog.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: It seems that the Firmus team took some of our previous feedback around health checks to an extreme, filling up the prolog with unnecessary dcgm level 3 checks when level 1, 2, or just an epilog with HealthCheckProgram configured would suffice.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: To their credit, a pre-staged nccl-test script was provided and ran at expected bandwidth.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: As mentioned previously, the Firmus monitoring stack is unique, going beyond standard DCGM metrics and feeding ML models to predict component failures before they occur.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: A “link flap” is formally defined as five events in one hour, triggering automated diagnostics.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Their internal validation suite is exhaustive, running regression tests on spare nodes that include P2P bandwidth tests, GDR copies, small-scale llama training runs, and NCCL tests to proactively identify GPUs, NVLink, or InfiniBand interconnects that are approaching failure.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: This level of investment in monitoring at the physical layer is how Firmus plans to back up an aggressive “99.94% SLA”, aiming to differentiate itself from competitors by ensuring maximum goodput – something that we have also heard from top-tier providers like CoreWeave and Nebius.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Their business model mirrors other major Nvidia clouds, with attractive prospective pricing for their upcoming rack-scale deployments, much of which is made possible by a low power cost in their massive expansion into Tasmania.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: We encourage Firmus to double-down on their focus on operational excellence from the physical layer to the orchestration layer (i.e. properly configured slurm and kubernetes clusters) without getting distracted by fancy PaaS and SaaS applications that the vendor-du-jour is pitching.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Fluidstack earns a ClusterMAX 2.0 Gold rating from SemiAnalysis.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Strong performance across all categories with minor gaps. Generally wins deals at competitive pricing.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Fluidstack is the only cloud to debut in our Gold tier this round, and certainly has the most unique business model.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Almost all of Fluidstack’s customer deployments involve a third-party datacenter provider.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Fluidstack is effectively the hired gun that organizations go to in order to turn bronze-tier datacenter infrastructure into a gold-tier customer experience.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Google has also gone into the market to [secure colocation demand](https://semianalysis.com/core-research/core-weekly-insights-6/) with Fluidstack as the operator of Terawulf and Cipher sites, potentially for their TPUs.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: This is clear when it comes to customers such as Meta, Poolside, Blackforest Labs, and an unnamed customer running in a TeraWulf datacenter in Buffalo that got a massive financial backstop from Google.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Our hands-on experience with Fluidstack was a live demonstration of their value proposition: a highly collaborative, deeply technical partnership that rapidly improves the platform based on expert feedback.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: While the initial cluster had rough edges, the speed and precision with which the Fluidstack team addressed every issue was unparalleled.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Our initial slurm cluster came with pyxis and MPI support integrated into srun, and initial two-node nccl-tests showed performance within range for large message sizes.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: However, we immediately hit a significant usability issue: the prolog.d script was so bloated with health checks that it took over a minute to schedule an interactive run on a single node.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: The script was running full single-node NCCL tests for NVLink and InfiniBand, plus host-to-device bandwidth checks, every time a job started.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: When we pointed this out, the team immediately acknowledged it and committed to their roadmap of moving these active health checks to run on idle nodes in the background, which is the standard practice for other top-tier providers.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: We noted that the Nvidia HPC-X toolkit was missing from the base image, which is necessary for optimal nccl performance at medium message sizes.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Within 24 hours, the Fluidstack team had deployed HPC-X to the base image on our cluster and added it to their standard deployment pipeline for all customers.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: The Grafana dashboard was solid, but we identified missing graphs for NVLink Rx/Tx utilization and incorrect DCGM metrics for tensor core pipes (they were capturing SIMT units instead of tensor core-specific pipes like DCGM_FI_PROF_PIPE_TENSOR_HMMA_ACTIVE).

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: The team implemented the correct DCGM metrics the following day.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Security Posture: This was the most critical finding.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: We discovered the cluster was running a version of the nvidia-container-toolkit vulnerable to NVIDIAScape (CVE-2025-23266).

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: The team patched the vulnerability on our cluster within minutes of us reporting it.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: While the immediate fix was impressive, our feedback focused on the larger operational need for automated dependency scanning and a proactive security process, such as enrolling in Nvidia’s security embargo program.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: We found that DCGM’s background health checks were not enabled.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: By injecting PCIe replay errors (dcgmi test --inject --gpuid 0 -f 202), we confirmed that the node would not automatically drain.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Our recommendation was to actively poll dcgmi health -c and configure NVIDIA Health Check (NHC) to drain nodes based on specific thresholds (e.g., >8 PCIe replays per minute or >100 NVLink CRC errors per second).

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: The team immediately added this to their near-term roadmap.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Transitioning to Kubernetes was seamless, with a kubeconfig readily available from the UI.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: The cluster provided a solid foundation with standard components like Cilium for CNI, a CSI w/ ReadWriteMany support, node-problem-detector, kube-prometheus-stack, draino, a custom controller to turn off ACS, and the Nvidia Network Operator + GPU Operator, all managed via ArgoCD.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: This high-touch model, typically involves shared Infrastructure-as-Code repos, ensuring customers get the exact tools they need, such as adding cert-manager in our case.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: This test, however, resurfaced the most critical theme from our slurm evaluation: software supply chain security.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: We discovered that the Nvidia GPU Operator chart was a minor version behind, leaving the cluster vulnerable to the same NVIDIAScape exploit.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: This highlighted a significant gap in their proactive security posture, particularly their absence from vendor embargo programs that provide advance notice of vulnerabilities.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Once notified, the team coordinated a maintenance window and patched the vulnerability in under an hour, and motivated them to formalize a security process that includes more frequent proactive updates, subscriptions to vulnerability databases, and taking steps to join Nvidia’s disclosure program.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Overall our experience with Fluidstack was strong.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: The platform was not perfect out-of-the-box, but both slurm and kubernetes were both in a perfectly usable state within hours of cluster handover, and the engineering team demonstrated an elite level of responsiveness and expertise.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Issues that might take weeks or months to get addressed in a hyperscaler’s ticketing system were fixed in hours.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: If there is anyone that demonstrated the “Forward Deployed Engineering” ethos during our testing, it was Fluidstack.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: FPT CLOUD earns a ClusterMAX 2.0 Unavailable rating from SemiAnalysis (updated April 2026 in the ClusterMAX 2.1 Update).

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: A large regional provider in Southeast Asia with significant capacity in Vietnam and Japan and partnerships throughout the region.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: We were unable to gain access to a cluster in time for publishing this article, but expect to include them in ClusterMAX 2.1 soon.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: We got the chance to test FPT Smart Cloud back in November 2025.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: FPT is based in Vietnam and at the time had H100 and H200 available.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: They use Soperator from Nebius for orchestration, and the cluster was well configured.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: We noticed some poor performance on the VAST Storage.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: The monitoring experience was quite strong, some of the best custom DCGM dashboards we have seen with Loki used for logging and analysis.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Unfortunately, FPT is held back from the silver tier due to some serious security issues.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Our testing showed that PKeys and SAKey were not configured correctly, allowing us to see every other endpoint on the network (i.e. every other customer).

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: GCORE earns a ClusterMAX 2.0 Silver rating from SemiAnalysis.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: GCORE is a Luxembourg-based provider that was founded in 2014, originally focusing on gaming, CDN, and general purpose cloud. But now, AI.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: GCORE offers GPUs across Europe, including datacenters in Luxembourg, Portugal, Germany, the Netherlands, the UK, and the US (Virginia and California).

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: They also have plans to go into the Nordics, partially via self-build, but also via an established partnership with Northern Data Group (also known as Taiga Cloud).

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: It’s unclear where this partnership will go, as Northern Data apparently just had their offices raided over tax fraud allegations related to crypto mining operations in 2023.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: The GCORE platform is feature rich, with a nice balance of usability and strong underlying hardware performance.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Unfortunately, only Kubernetes was available to test for us.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: We learned after the fact that their Slurm-on-Kubernetes offering, based on SOperator, is [buried in API documentation](https://gcore.com/docs/api-reference/cloud/managed-kubernetes/create-k8s-cluster#body-add-ons-slurm). We look forward to testing this in the future.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: The onboarding process began with a series of manual hurdles where we quickly realized we were dealing with an enterprise-ready console modeled after the hyperscalers.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: After creating an account, we were required to request a quota increase to spin up a cluster.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: This actually resulted in us needing to make three separate attempts (over the course of two working days) to get quota approved for 2TiB of VAST Storage to go with our 2-node kubernetes cluster.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Forging ahead, we followed the required steps: creating a three virtual networks, a VPC, provisioning our Kubernetes cluster, which promptly became stuck in a “provisioning” state for over two hours before ultimately failing.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Notably, GCORE takes networking seriously: routers, configurable networks, floating IPs, firewalls, and reserved IPs. It can just make things confusing on setup for non-cloud native users.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Our second attempt was more successful, at least on the surface. The cluster spun-up correctly, including a default ReadWriteMany StorageClass using the VAST quota we fought so hard for.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Unfortunately, the cluster was delivered without the Nvidia GPU Operator or the Network Operator.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: This is a critical point for many general-purpose clouds that have kubernetes experience but miss some of the basics when they turn to serving the AI market.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: After confirming that performance on nccl-tests, a torchtitan pretraining job, and disaggregated prefill/decode inference endpoints via llm-d was working as expected we turned to focus on monitoring. Unfortunately, this seems to be left completely up to the user.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: While gold and platinum tier providers handle the CNI, CSI, active/passive health checks (e.g. via node-problem-detector or custom controllers and CRDs), kube-prometheus-stack (i.e. on a Grafana dashboard), and Slurm-on-Kubernetes, GCORE leaves that all that stuff up to the user.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Overall, GCORE’s platform is strong, and one of the best purely self-service offerings we tried for kubernetes.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: The console includes all the enterprise goodies one would expect, and it makes sense why this enable them to sell into large enterprise with PCI DSS compliance and a global datacenter footprint.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: We encourage GCORE to develop an advanced cluster monitoring dashboard, implement active/passive health checks on the kubernetes layer, and consider developing a first-class Slurm-on-Kubernetes experience over time.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: GMI earns a ClusterMAX 2.0 Bronze rating from SemiAnalysis.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: GMI is our top Bronze neocloud that is just not quite there yet.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: The company shows promise, with recent developments like achieving security compliance and implementing confidential computing capabilities for H100 and H200 nodes.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: However, in our testing the slurm cluster was frankly unusable.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: We did not get access to a self-service console or monitoring dashboard of any kind, and it took over a month from our initial request, and multiple follow ups to finally login.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: On the cluster, slurmctld was running directly on a compute node, and the environment was missing basic tools like docker the modules utility.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: More critically, the cluster was provisioned without a shared home directory across nodes despite having VAST with POSIX/NFS and S3 options in the environment.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: After negotiating to get a shared fs configured on the cluster, we found that the performance was terrible. Basic file-saving operations and carriage returns in the terminal would take multiple seconds to complete or respond.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: One of our GMI nodes, with 1.9TB of shared storage, and 27.9TB of local storage, matching NVIDIA’s DGX specification perfectly

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: On the positive side, the underlying hardware appears to be configured correctly for high-performance workloads.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: A check for nvidia_peermem confirmed that GPUDirect RDMA is enabled, and the team confirmed that their interconnect network is built on InfiniBand with PKeys for network segmentation.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: We also found no evidence of active or passive health checks, and no monitoring dashboards were provided to give visibility into cluster state or job performance.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: In the future, when we can confirm that the Slurm offering is working well, development of monitoring dashboards is complete, active and passive health checks are in place, and a comprehensive Kubernetes offering is available, we expect GMI to be an obvious candidate to move into the silver tier.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: GMO Cloud earns a ClusterMAX 2.0 Silver rating from SemiAnalysis.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Adequate offering with noticeable gaps compared to Gold or Platinum. Room for improvement.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: GMO Cloud, part of the sprawling Japanese conglomerate GMO Internet Group, presents a highly opinionated approach targeting their domestic market.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: The offering is built on a foundation of security that for us is so stringent it alters the user experience, while still providing solid performance.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: We focused on slurm as kubernetes is not available, and quickly found that sinfo and scontrol are completely disabled for end-users.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: This decision, presumably made in the name of security, caused us issues with pre-baked scripts that depend on scontrol show hostnames $SLURM_JOB_NODELIST and other basic convenience functions.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: It also resulted in us having to modify some of our standard debugging practices, since users are unable to inspect the cluster state or topology.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Thankfully, GMO provides a convenience command “snodes”, and a custom script, “get_master_addr.sh” which got us running jobs at expected performance.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: GMO did not configure topology.conf, relying on a rationale that since they manually allocate customer clusters to servers that do not span across different Spectrum-X leaf switches, and organize everything by known hostnames, they are able to make topology awareness at the slurm level redundant.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: We think this points to a lack of experience running large customer clusters, and handling hardware failures in large multi-tenant environments.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: The environment lacks support for Pyxis and Enroot, effectively blocking teams that have standardized on Docker-based containers.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Users are required to rebuild their entire workflow around Singularity, a relatively significant undertaking that creates another barrier to entry for new users.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Unfortunately, this focus on security can also fall short at a basic level, creating a strange paradox.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: On the other, we found outdated packages, such as nvidia-container-toolkit versions 1.16.2 and 1.17.4 on login and compute nodes respectively.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: While GMO acknowledges these are flagged by their internal vulnerability scanners and slated for an update, the presence of old software vulnerable to 9.0 Critical CVE’s running on our brand-new cluster contrasts sharply with the user-facing restrictions.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Overall, GMO’s approach feels like security theater to us.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: On the positive side, the base environment is well-configured for HPC tasks.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: The nodes come pre-installed and configured with HPC-X, NCCL, and nvcc making it dead simple to build nccl-tests from source and run it at full expected bandwidth.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: We were also able to run torchtitan jobs at expected MFU.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: In addition, the standard dcgmi health -c program is configured properly as a Slurm HealthCheckProgram, addressing our background health check expectations.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Finally, the platform lacks key observability and reliability features.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: There is no monitoring dashboard, though GMO states a Grafana-based solution is planned for a future release.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: For now, users must rely on basic Slurm email notifications for job status, and we could not identify any proactive health check system, placing the burden of failure detection largely on the user.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Overall, GMO has established a clear advantage within Japan, especially with the region’s dependence on Slurm and other traditional HPC technologies.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Support is strong, and we expect that example customers like Turing: <https://group.gmo/news/article/9501/> and AI Robot Association (AIRoA) <https://internet.gmo/en/news/article/45/> trust the offering as GMO Cloud is a leader domestically.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: We recommend that GMO focus on usability over security theatre, improve monitoring options for users via custom Grafana dashboard, improve passive and active health checks, and consider developing a kubernetes offering in the future.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Google Cloud (GCP) earns a ClusterMAX 2.0 Silver rating from SemiAnalysis.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: You would think Google would set the standard.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: We have to pull CoreWeave containers from gcr to run on their kubernetes cluster.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Since the first version of this article, Google has addressed some issues holding them back, specifically making the decision to go with standard CX-7 NICs for their H200 (a3-mega) and B200 (a3-ultra) instances, as well as their GB200 NVL72 instances (a4).

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Our testing began by provisioning clusters for both slurm and Kubernetes (GKE).

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: The managed slurm “Cluster Director” offering is still in preview, though at Google “preview” also means that key customers have had it for several months, and things work well.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: The architecture follows a standard managed service model where the slurmctld is handled by GCP, leaving users with access to the login and worker nodes.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: We appreciated the default setup, including scripts for testing network performance via nccl-test and storage performance via FIO pre-staged in a GCS bucket for immediate use.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: For storage, GCP recommends Filestore for home directories, which provides enterprise features like snapshots and backups, while managed Lustre is positioned for large-scale, high-performance scratch space.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Provisioning our Lustre filesystem was straightforward but not instant, taking roughly 40 minutes to complete.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Interestingly, the cluster also demonstrated self-healing capabilities; when we intentionally deleted a worker node to clean things up and move from slurm to GKE testing, the Cluster Director service automatically recreated it in a matter of minutes to maintain the desired capacity.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: However, the GKE-based solution is where GCP truly shines and feels years ahead of all Neocloud competition but CoreWeave.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)

quote: Google and Nvidia have said that they have started to look into this and have plans on how to improve it.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: While the company has deep experience in building dedicated HPC clusters, this has not yet translated into a polished, user-friendly cloud console, or cluster monitoring experience.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Their product offerings feel conflicted with a new-mslurm, old-mslurm, new-mk8s, old-mk8s, private cloud, 1-Click Cluster, and on-demand Instances.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Notably, 1-Click Clusters aren’t really one click, as you need to wait for approval.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: For users that want an on-demand machines instantly, Lambda is generally considered to be the top-tier on-demand provider, with the largest fleet of GPUs available.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: However, in our recent experience, Lambda is in fact suffering from success in on-demand. We are generally met with greyed-out screens showing that capacity is sold-out:

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Also, for a hot minute, Lambda appeared to be getting into the serverless inference API endpoint business, which would put them in direct competition with some of their largest customers. But that is no longer:

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Overall, we like the focus. Lambda has pivoted, and is very focused on their 1-Click-Cluster (1CC) business, focusing on “big game hunting”.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: During our testing, we evaluated both their new (self-managed) and old (rancher-based) Kubernetes offerings, and their newly available slurm offering. Neither of these is UI or CLI driven, instead requiring a Lambda engineer to set up the cluster for you.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Lambda’s Kubernetes product feels like an early-stage offering, marked by technical debt and a challenging user experience.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: While the current product does not use Rancher, the public documentation still references it, causing initial confusion.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: The user experience for inference workloads is particularly lacking. Clusters do not come with a default public IP solution (like MetalLB or an external LoadBalancer).

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: While documentation exists for a simple, single-GPU vLLM deployment, there are no examples for multi-GPU, multi-node, or auto-scaling inference workloads.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: For monitoring, Lambda uses a mix of open-source tools, including LeptonAI’s gpud for GPU device management and node-problem-detector for health checks, but the integration is not seamless into their monitoring dashboards for the new or old mk8s products.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Dashboards are easy to access, but missing integration to the metrics without an install of an agent that is not documented, and upon further inspection, still in development.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: For slurm, Lambda’s offering is a more recent addition, and the onboarding process was fraught with issues.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: The initial setup process was cumbersome: ssh keys were not correctly provisioned on the cluster, the default home directory was not shared across nodes by default, requiring data to be moved manually.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: New user account creation is a headache, requiring workarounds like unsetting environment variables (XDG_DATA_HOME) to function correctly.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: To their credit, once these initial hurdles were overcome, the cluster’s performance was strong. We observed expected allreduce, allgather and alltoall bandwidth on nccl-tests and were able to achieve full MFU on an example torchtitan training workloads.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: For example, a welcome message (which was invisible in some SSH clients like Cursor or VSCode) contained custom instructions for a grafana-access command to quickly view performance metrics.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Lambda’s approach to reliability on the slurm cluster included a custom dcgm-status script, which can be run on-demand:

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: The script is also scheduled to run on a regular cadence in a low-priority, “preemptible” partition:

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: We were impressed by Lambda’s commitment to developing comprehensive active and passive health checks, and believe that they are well on their way to improving reliability challenges, and building the battle scars necessary to run NVL72 rack-scale systems at scale.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: With that said, some of the access issues we encountered point to broader operational challenges at Lambda. Their cloud console (though not our cluster) experienced outages during our brief testing window.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Internally, there appears to be a general degree of disorganization.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: When asked about a true “cloud console” experience, Lambda acknowledged that the team’s background is primarily in traditional HPC cluster deployment, not building scalable, self-service cloud infrastructure.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: On the positive side, Lambda is actively working on improving its platform based on our feedback.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: They have a compliance team addressing SOC 2 Type II requirements for individual sites, and are working to implement both SHARP and InfiniBand security keys for multi-tenant isolation, following recent Nvidia recommendations (and, likely, the onboarding of Nvidia as a customer with a $1.5B contract).

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Their storage offerings primarily focus on VAST, with future S3-compatible offerings currently in development.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Overall, Lambda is a strong provider with deep hardware expertise, massive capacity, and big plans for the future. However, their public cloud product feels immature, and engaging with the team feels chaotic.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: We encourage Lambda to continue to work on translating their HPC hardware prowess into a stable, easy-to-use, and reliable cloud service.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Latitude.sh earns a ClusterMAX 2.0 Bronze rating from SemiAnalysis.

quote: Latitude.sh presents itself as a straightforward provider with bare metal or virtual L40S and H100 machines mostly located in Dallas, Texas.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Upon logging in, the console is clean and well-organized.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: We appreciate the ability to organize resources by project and apply tags for environments like ‘dev’ or ‘pre-prod’.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: An interesting and somewhat unique feature is the ‘Cloud Gateway’ service, which leverages Megaport to establish private connections to major public clouds.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Beyond the individual instance issues, Latitude has no Slurm or Kubernetes offerings, no integrated monitoring dashboards, no shared storage options, and no health checks.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: For individual developers or small teams, Latitude.sh might offer a compelling price point.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: But for organizations seeking a production-ready cluster, the platform falls short.

quote: Lightning.ai earns a ClusterMAX 2.0 Bronze rating from SemiAnalysis.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Meets minimum criteria. Last category we directly recommend; often with inconsistent support or networking gaps.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Lightning.ai (aka Lightning Cloud) is a broker for GPU machines in neoclouds and hyperscalers that provides useful MLOps features on top.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: The founding story of Lightning Cloud begins with the development of PyTorch Lightning, an open-source framework that organizes and simplifies boilerplate PyTorch code such as the training loop, logging, checkpointing, and distributed training.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: The lightning git repo seems to be the #1 way top-of-funnel sales start for Lightning Cloud.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Older frameworks like NVIDIA NeMo use Lightning under the hood, while new frameworks that we use in our testing such as torchtitan, verifiers and Megatron-LM do not.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: The open source `pytorch-lightning` and `lightning` packages are still growing rapidly:

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Functionally, the Lightning Cloud product offers a simple way to track who’s using what across multiple clouds.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: We had a chance to test the Lightning Studio, which provides access to GPUs in a browser (VSCode, Jupyter notebook) or remote SSH (VSCode, Cursor, Windsurf, etc).

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Our testing of clusters is coming soon.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Notably, these multi-GPU studios, batch jobs, and mmt training jobs are restricted to users on a Pro, Teams or Enterprise Custom payment tier.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Lightning is the only neocloud we have seen charging a per-seat price, and translating that into GPU-hrs behind the scenes on clusters that they manage for the customer.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Interestingly, there is an easy way to attach/detach GPUs to existing “studios” (i.e. notebooks or remote shells) and auto-sleep them if unused.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: This means that users only paying for what they use.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Lightning also forecasts the wait times associated with spinning up a GPU from a given provider, such as AWS, Google, Lambda, Voltage Park, or Nebius.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: The worst wait time is for an 8x H200 machine in AWS, estimated at 3hrs.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Unfortunately, despite what the website says, there are no GPUs available from NScale.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Another piece that jumped out during testing is that notebooks have full CLI access including docker, meaning the notebook is running directly on a VM under the hood.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: This leaves users with full flexibility in the environment.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Overall we have our doubts about the utility of remote developer environments where cluster access is abstracted away from users, especially at the high-end of the market.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: The largest buyers of GPU compute do not have a problem spinning up a notebook on kubernetes with a simple manifest.yaml, or accessing a single machine via `srun -N1 —gpus-per-node=8 —pty bash` in a slurm cluster.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: We find it hard to see a path forward for Lightning Cloud if the industry moves beyond the lightning framework and the GPU marketplace business continues to focus on taking a margin on top of expensive hyperscalers, with no third party compute.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: As for the ClusterMAX rating system, we look forward to testing Lightning Cloud’s mmt training, and kubernetes in the future.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: We encourage Lightning to consider building a slurm offering, adding monitoring dashboards for underlying cluster health that integrates with job logs and performance profiling, adding integration with active/passive health checks on clusters, and customization options for high performance storage and networking.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Mithril/ML Foundry earns a ClusterMAX 2.0 Underperforming rating from SemiAnalysis.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Mithril (formerly ML Foundry, formerly Foundry) operates as a GPU aggregator, or what they term an “AI omnicloud.”

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Their core philosophy is that the primary problem in the GPU market is one of price discovery and market inefficiency.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Their solution is to create a “fluid market” through aggregation and abstraction, allowing costs to adjust dynamically to reflect increased supply. We completely disagree with both the premise and solution.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: The premise that the GPU market lacks price discover is flawed and represents a fundamental misunderstanding of the market.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: In our experience, over 90% of the GPU cloud rental volume is done on long-term contract between enterprises with a standard 25% down and monthly payments through the end of the term.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Mithril, and other companies trying to aggressively financialize the GPU market as though it is crude oil or lumber, is solving for price per GPU-hr as the only variable.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: This is an important criteria, but it is just one the 129 criteria that we use to assess a provider’s quality, and is often a poor proxy for the realized TCO of a cluster.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: By building abstractions on top of an aggregated and abstracted “roll-of-the-dice” marketplace of underlying providers, Mithril places the entire operational burden on the end user.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: As a provider, Mithril has no control over their customer’s support experience, orchestration software preferences, networking and storage performance, monitoring experience, or, most critically, the reliability and security posture of the cluster.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: With that said, even if GPU compute was a liquid, commoditized market, we would expect the winner to have open access to many GPU providers, real-time data feeds on availability, forecasts for upcoming supply, proxy information for realized quality from end users… but unfortunately we are left with this instead:

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)

quote: Naver s effectively the “Google of South Korea”, thanks to their success in search, blogging, forums, e-commerce, payments and more.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
