speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: We look forward to testing Naver’s GPU cloud offerings in the future.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Nebius earns a ClusterMAX 2.0 Gold rating from SemiAnalysis.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Since ClusterMAX 1.0, Nebius has continued to show up as the most direct competitor to CoreWeave in our customer conversations.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Nebius counts customers such as Shopify, Recraft, Mirage, Genesis Therapeutics, and most recently landed a 5-year $17.4B deal (with expansion to $19.4B) with Microsoft for their Vineland, New Jersey datacenter.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: the healthy deal pipeline sugests more incremental capacity coming online over time.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Nebius differentiates financially due to its low cost of capital, with billions on its balance sheet, no debt, and a strong position as one of two publicly traded GPU-only Neoclouds that we track (the other being CoreWeave).

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Nebius differentiates technically with a virtualized approach to GPU infrastructure (built on experience from Yandex), and an AI-native approach due to their dogfood approach with their internal AI team, that has resulted in multiple spinoff startups in the AI space.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: While we are aware of their struggles in securing colocation deals and establishing a credit rating, their engineering prowess is evident.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: The Nebius platform prioritizes flexibility, on-demand access, and a robust Kubernetes-native experience. This stands in contrast to CoreWeave’s bare metal, long-term reservation model and makes Nebius a compelling choice for autoscaling and spot instances, specifically used for experimentation and inference.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Nebius continues to show up as a low-cost provider on various marketplaces, and as the infrastructure, and is one of the only providers with realistic pricing right on the homepage of their website.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: As if that wasn’t enough, Nebius is also foraying into the inference endpoint market!

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Since ClusterMAX 1.0, Nebius has officially launched their [managed Soperator service](https://nebius.com/blog/posts/introducing-managed-soperator) for a fully self-service Slurm-on-Kubernetes experience.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: We were able to test this out, and as expected we got a Slurm cluster that was completely set up and ready for use out of the box.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: This included pre-installed drivers, Docker, passwordless SSH between nodes, and expected performance on collectives (nccl-tests) and pytorch training jobs (torchtitan pretraining) out-of-the-box.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Later in the article we will describe how difficult it is for other providers to install Slurm-on-Kubernetes (via Soperator or Slinky) with good defaults.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: they completely control the roadmap and are vertically integrated from customer support issues in an sbatch script, down to the kubernetes orchestration, hardware, and datacenter troubleshooting layers.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: The control plane also looks nice:

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Unlike CoreWeave’s bare-metal-first strategy, Nebius has built its platform on layers of Kubernetes clusters managing each other, using KubeVirt all the way down.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: This means that customer workloads, even for full 8-GPU nodes, run inside virtual machines on a kubernetes cluster that they can access, which itself is managed by a kubernetes cluster that only Nebius can access. This design is similar to how GCP orchestrates compute.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: For example, they use virtio-fs to attach a massive shared root filesystem, which presented as 197TB out-of-the box in our cluster, mounted at “/”, but obviously does not require 197TB of drives to be physically installed in the servers themselves.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Nebius’s storage solution is built on YDB <https://ydb.tech/docs/en/contributor/distributed-storage> , which actually underpins their block, shared filesystem, and storage offerings.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: This approach to storage has reduced startup times (i.e. pulling a container image or model file) for new machines with some example on-demand autoscaling workloads from over 10 minutes to around 2-3 minutes.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: When we raised this, the Nebius team was adamant that users should simply benchmark the platform. Their position is that because there is no virtualization layer for the InfiniBand fabric or the NvidiaGPUs themselves, performance should be identical to bare metal.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Our initial testing seems to validate this claim, and third party results do too. For example, in the last round of MLPerf Inference v5.1 benchmarks, Nebius achieved top tier performance on Nvidia GB200 NVL72, HGX B200 and HGX H200 systems, for inference with Llama models.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: An additional note that customers have expressed with VMs is the ability to easily enable low-level hardware counters for performance monitoring. The method for enabling hardware counters varies by virtualization platform.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: However, on KubeVirt (which Nebius uses) via KVM/QEMU, the VMs inherit the capability to expose hardware counters from the underlying host.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Notably, for very large customers who insist on it and are doing a long-term rental, Nebius does have an option to provide bare metal clusters.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Initially, our access to monitoring was a simple Grafana dashboard available via an SSH port forward. These metrics and health checks were basic, but the team later released a series of updates that raised the bar significantly.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Interestingly, since all of this is being integrated into SOperator, and Soperator is open source, we have been able to watch the roadmap come to life on the Soperator GitHub project

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: There is no other Neocloud as open and transparent with their development as Nebius.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Nebius also released a blog post describing what they do for reliability in detail: on-site factory tests, node deployment tests, virtual platform tests, pre-provisioning cluster tests, passive and active health checks.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: We believe this suite of burn-in tests, checks, and monitoring dashboards will improve cluster reliability and usability, especially as Nebius moves to adopting the GB300 NVL72 rack-scale systems at scale, for customers such as Microsoft.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: In the blog, Nebius describes a hypothetical example with 13 failures over 336 hours (14 days) on a 1,024 GPU cluster, resulting in a GPU-level MTBF of 26,446 GPU-hr, or 1,101 GPU-days.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: An apt comparison for this is to the data from Meta’s Llama 3 paper, which claims 419 failures over 1,296 hours (55 days) on a 16,000 GPU cluster, resulting in a GPU-level MTBF of 50,677 GPU-hr, or 2,111 GPU-days.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: As a further comparison, we have heard from customers that run similar scale clusters (1k to 2k GPUs) from gold and silver tier providers experience as much as 5+ failures per day, for extended periods of time. This translates to a GPU-level MTBF of less than 10,000 GPU-hr, or less than 400 GPU-days.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Meanwhile the hypotheical number from Nebius tracks as a reasonably good customer experience.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Later in the blog, Nebius claims to have had single 3,000 GPU cluster operate uninterrupted for 169,800 GPU hours or 56.6 hours of stable operation. This would translate to an absurdly high GPU-level MTBF of 169,800 GPU-hours or 7,000 days. We are generally frustrated by providers who cherry-pick reliability data in this manner.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: We encourage customers to track this reliability data for themselves, especially if DataDog, New Relic, Splunk, or a custom Prometheus Alertmanager is setup and connected to a slack channel for notifications on XID related errors.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: It is clear that Nebius is building battle scars when it comes to managed slurm clusters at the 1k+ GPU scale.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: A key differentiator for Nebius is their robust support for on-demand and autoscaling workloads. This is a direct result of their software-defined architecture.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: They offer pre-emptible instances, primarily for inference customers, which function similarly to spot instances on hyperscalers. This allows users to access capacity at a lower cost, with the understanding that the workload can be interrupted.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: We’ve seen public examples of this in action, such as Shopify’s work with SkyPilot and dstack sky on the Nebius platform, which highlights their strength in supporting dynamic, research-oriented workloads.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: This flexibility is a significant advantage for users who cannot commit to long-term contracts, and seems to be a major source of inbound customer qualification for Nebius.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Their deep investment in a Kubernetes-native, virtualized stack using KubeVirt and Soperator allows them to offer a degree of flexibility and on-demand access that is rare in the high-performance training space.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: While they may face headwinds in datacenter acquisition, their software stack is mature and performant.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Our feedback to Nebius is to continue improving their monitoring and health-check visibility as they roll these updates out to customers, and to streamline the notification process for all tiers of users.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Their ability to deliver bare-metal-equivalent performance through a VM-based architecture is a significant engineering achievement.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: For users whose needs revolve around research, autoscaling inference, and workloads that can benefit from a spot-like pre-emptible market, Nebius is an excellent choice that challenges the long-term reservation model of its competitors.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Notably, some customers have been fixated on Nebius’ Russian roots, despite the fact that all of their staff are based outside of Russia, as opposed to making purchasing decisions on technical merits. We’re not sure how Nebius can address customers that hold this mindset.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Neev Cloud earns a ClusterMAX 2.0 Unavailable rating from SemiAnalysis.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Neev Cloud is another Indian neocloud that unfortunately did not want us to test their offerings depite plans to deploy 40,000 GPUs by 2026 in their Indore location in Central India, backed by a $1.5B investment.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: An initial order in mid-2024 was placed for 8,000 GPUs from HPE, with planned expansion to Chennai, Mumbai, Hyderabad and Noida.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: The website claims 1000 to 16000 GPUs connected with InfiniBand, with H200, B200 and B300 all available for “pre-reservation”.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: A prominent picture of the Neev Cloud CEO shaking hands with Modi on their front page leaves us to assume that Neev will be serving sovereign Indian customers primarily.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: However, it seems that kubernetes and slurm clusters are not available for testing.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: India is a large country with a vibrant tech ecosystem, but it is unclear how many neoclouds will make it going forward.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Neysa earns a ClusterMAX 2.0 Bronze rating from SemiAnalysis.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Neysa is an emerging provider operating in the Indian market.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: They have recently signed an MoU with NTT Data and the Telangana government to build a 400MW, 25k GPU facility in Hyderabad, and currently operate a fleet of H100, H200, and soon MI300X AMD GPUs.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: However, our testing revealed that their current platform has gaps in security and usability when compared to international competitors.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: The onboarding process raised concerns on security for us.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Access is managed via username and password-based SSH, with manual IP address filtering and a fragmented user account system.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: We had no way to create new users for others on the team to test, implying that it would be difficult to support RBAC with an external IAM provider.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: The SLURM environment itself also suffered from basic configuration errors.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Jobs fail to run initially as no default partition is configured, requiring manual specification for every submission.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: In addition there was no topology.conf configured.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: If Neya is going to run a 25k GPU cluster in the future, topology aware scheduling is going to be critical.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Also, monitoring and health checks are effectively non-existent.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: The provided Grafana dashboard was non-functional during our testing and appeared to be missing some expected exporters for health checks or performance monitoring to work.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: On a more positive note, the software stack for containerized workloads is modern. We found an up-to-date NVIDIA container toolkit, and both pyxis and enroot were installed.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: At the time of testing, Neysa did not have a Kubernetes offering available for us to test.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: We expect Neysa to benefit from compliance with Indian regulations such as the DPDP, but we find it unlikely that they are able expand beyond their domestic market at this time.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: We encourage Neysa to improve their default experience: a better security posture, user management, proactive support experience, default monitoring systems, and health checks.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: NScale earns a ClusterMAX 2.0 Unavailable rating from SemiAnalysis.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: NScale is an NVIDIA-backed partner with a huge presence in Stargate Norway, which we have covered extensively in our Datacenter Model

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: They have announced multi-billion contracts with Microsoft, with the first one in September and follow up with a subsequent announcement in October.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: These deployments are for Nvidia’s GB300 rack scale solutions.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Unfortunately we have been unable to gain access to any GPUs on the NScale platform, either directly or through publicly advertised partners like Lightning.ai.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: We regret the difficulties and look forward to testing NScale services in the future.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Oracle earns a ClusterMAX 2.0 Gold rating from SemiAnalysis.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Oracle just posted the most incredible quarterly earnings the market has ever seen.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Specifically, Oracle signed four multi-billion-dollar contracts with three different customers in Q1, including a $300Bn+ deal with OpenAI.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Recent release from The Information suggested AI server margin concerns from these multi-billion contracts, but we think lower margin during a ramp up period makes sense and

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Oracle is in a unique position as the only hyperscaler (over 100 AD’s across 45 active regions globally) without an in-house AGI Research program or significant venture capital investment (though Larry did invest $2B in xAI after a few texts from Elon) which has led them to land contracts with OpenAI, Meta, ByteDance, and Nvidia.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: They currently have over 60% of US Stargate according to public releases.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Oracle also pivoted to wholesale bare metal early, taking advantage of their balance sheet while also maintaining a notable presence in the managed slurm and managed kubernetes market.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: In many cases, we have found other cloud providers giving us servers with IP addresses, locations, and other configuration information that makes it clear we’re actually running in an Oracle datacenter.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Oracle’s default setup is typically provisioned through the console, using Terraform for automation behind the scenes.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: A notable point of friction for some users is the almost-mandatory use of Oracle Linux (version 8.10 by default), which is based on Fedora.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: This operating system choice is contentious, as many AI workloads, particularly those in the open-source community, are first tested on Debian-based operating systems, specifically Ubuntu, for its broad compatibility and ease of use.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: We attribute this default to Oracle Linux as a historical beef with Canonical. This is surprising given that certified Ubuntu images have been available on Oracle Bare Metal Cloud Services since 2017 and are current modern to version 24.04.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: In order to deploy a slurm or kubernetes cluster through the OCI console, users unfortunately need to use the OCI console.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Visually, the console adheres to the [Redwood design system](https://redwood.oracle.com/), and uses their [JavaScript Extension Toolkit (JET)](https://www.oracle.com/webfolder/technetwork/jet/index.html), both of which do not spark joy.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: After deploying a cluster, users who want to access a Grafana dashboard will need to navigate the maze of UI element options at their disposal.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: During testing of both slurm and Kubernetes, everything went smoothly. We were able to quickly achieve expected collective bandwidth on nccl-tests, and expected MFU on torchtitan.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Interestingly, upon first login to the slurm cluster we found a single node in a drain state. This was quickly replaced, but highlighted the difference in approaches to health checks and bare metal node provisioning when compared to CoreWeave.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Node Auto-Repair and Node Problem Detector integration is expected in Q4, with the goal of providing customers with a “doctor HPC” user experience via an official OCI binary.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: The team is also developing an Active Health Check mechanism called the Sustained Workflow Check, which involves running PyTorch and CUDA matmul linear regressions for 2-5 minutes to ensure sustained performance.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: This check is currently running on-demand, and in most cases an Oracle engineer works directly with customers to schedule the checks in a low-priority partition. Default behaviour is being developed to integrate this into both slurm and OKE.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: For managed Kubernetes, Oracle offers OKE (Oracle Container Engine for Kubernetes), with all resources being public by default.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: OKE provides GPU and GPU+RDMA pools as provisioning options, along with integrated storage options via a checkbox. The official instructions for setting up RDMA are publicly available, and nccl-test manifests show good out-of-the-box performance for allreduce and allgather operations.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: A key point of frustration in the OKE setup is the lack of a direct kubeconfig file. Users are instead required to SSH into the cluster to perform management functions.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: On OKE, Oracle does not deploy the full GPU Operator but rather the device plugin only, with plans to add the full operator later.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Performance testing on kubernetes using vllm benchmarks for pd disaggregation with llm-d showed strong results, and was easy to setup and integrate with provided LoadBalancer services via public IP.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: The initial testing phase suffered from a lack of integrated health checks. While slurm metrics were added later, the control plane initially lacked the necessary CLI features, which required some rollbacks to prevent customers from inadvertently terminating jobs.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: The introduction of a new “mgmt” CLI aims to address these operational complexities and we agree.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: For Storage, Oracle offers a robust marketplace, with Weka and DDN being the primary partners.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Oracle customers report that the shared support experience is stronger with Weka on Oracle than with either VAST or DDN.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: For Networking, Oracle is like any other hyperscaler talking their book, trying to convince large customers that InfiniBand is not the only high-performance network solution, and their RoCE works well. They seem to be making progress in this regard.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Overall, Oracle has made significant progress improving their managed cluster offerings, with improved monitoring dashboards and node lifecycle management, but there is still room to improve in terms of proactivity.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: There is still a chance that customers will discover a bad node before Oracle’s automated systems, and have to report the node for replacement manually.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Oracle continues to be the most cost-effective of the four hyperscalers, and stands out as deploying new infrastructure the quickest, while also providing the best support.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: We expect Oracle to continue to grow both their wholesale bare metal and managed cluster business going forward, and we encourage Oracle to maintain its commitment to excellent customer support for all customers.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: OVHcloud earns a ClusterMAX 2.0 Underperforming rating from SemiAnalysis.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: As one of Europe’s largest cloud providers, OVHcloud has a massive footprint and lots of experience.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: They should be well positioned to capture the sovereign AI market in the EEA.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: However, OVH is still defined by a legacy IaaS/VPS model that lacks modern GPUs and, oh I don’t know, [that one time their Strasbourg datacenter burnt down](https://corporate.ovhcloud.com/en/newsroom/news/informations-site-strasbourg/).

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Source: the most modern GPU available at OVH is an H100 PCIe (for £2.41 at that)

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: PaleBlueDot earns a ClusterMAX 2.0 Underperforming rating from SemiAnalysis.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: PaleBlueDot is one of the many marketplaces covered in the underperforming tier that is missing a basic security attestation.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: We had a good experience testing some of the five different clouds that are aggregated on the PaleBlueDot marketplace.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: It was easy to spin up and connect to virtual machines, and we were only charged by the minute.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: We encourage PaleBlueDot to consider onboarding more providers in order to increase GPU availability and provide a true cluster experience via slurm or kubernetes orchestration and shared storage.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Prime Intellect earns a ClusterMAX 2.0 Bronze rating from SemiAnalysis.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Meets minimum criteria. Last category we directly recommend; often with inconsistent support or networking gaps.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Prime Intellect is our favourite non-neocloud startup that happens to be a neocloud too.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Prime is most well known for their decentralized training runs (INTELLECT) and synthetic dataset generation (SYNTHETIC).

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: They have also debuted an environments hub, quickly becoming the go-to place for researchers interested in open source RL environments.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: We absolutely love Prime’s open source contributions: Verifiers (a library for creating RL environments), PCCL (a library for running collectives over TCP/IP, i.e. on the WAN), and PRIME-RL (a framework for asynchronous RL at scale).

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: For our testing, we were provided with a 4-node SLURM cluster, a feature that was still in beta at the time.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: We gave initial feedback on some configuration issues: no shared home directory, no passwordless ssh, preinstalled MPI, lmod, container toolkit, pyxis or enroot.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Initial attempts to launch batch jobs failed due to InvalidAccount errors, and distributed PyTorch runs via torchrun hung on hostname resolution, suggesting some networking issues.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: We also saw a lack of health checks or dcgmi integration, and no monitoring dashboard available.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: After these findings, the prime team was all over it and completely overhauled the configuration.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: In less than a day, they added passwordless ssh, docker with nct, enroot, pyxis, the nvidia hpc sdk (nvcc, mpirun, hpcx), aliasing for python3, preinstalled uv, and a custom controller-hosted nfs mount for /home directories.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Prime Intellect’s responsiveness was among the biggest thing we took away from the engagement.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: We were able to go from sending feedback in slack to a working cluster in a matter of hours.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: In the future, we look forward to further validation of their slurm offering for topology-aware scheduling, automated health checks, monitoring dashboards, and large-scale I/O performance.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: We are aware of some large customers have have taken the plunge, running clusters at the 1k GPU scale with Prime outside of their public console and marketplace.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: We are also very excited for the launch of a kubernetes offering, coming soon.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Overall, if the team at Prime keeps up their relentless pace of shipping new features, we expect them to quickly move higher in the ClusterMAX rankings.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Qubrid earns a ClusterMAX 2.0 Bronze rating from SemiAnalysis.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Qubrid enters our ratings in the Bronze tier.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: The provider offers individual GPU instances (VMs) and bare-metal server rentals through a clean web console, with hardware ranging from H100s to the latest B200s.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Our hands-on testing of their individual VM offering was a mixed bag.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: On the positive side, the user experience for provisioning a single machine is straightforward.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: SSH and Jupyter access are easy to configure, and our B200 instance was provisioned and accessible in around 8 minutes.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: However, this basic usability is undermined by the fact that Qubrid charges users while the machine is stuck spinning up.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: We can only speculate that the reason for this is that Qubrid is running on AWS hardware in Ashburn, VA (us-east) as confirmed by a basic IP test when we logged in, though they do not make this clear to their customers.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Readers can see in the screenshot above that our B200 instance was provisioned with the CUDA 12.4 toolkit by default.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: While the driver was newer (12.6), this older toolkit just obviously doesn’t work with Blackwell hardware (i.e. SM100) which requires CUDA 12.8 or above.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Finally, Qubrid’s business model feels more like a traditional server host than a flexible neocloud.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Their pricing requires strict minimum commitments (e.g., 1-week for H100, 1-month for H200, and 3-months for B200) and they openly advertise yearly server rentals, despite not owning the hardware.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: We encourage Qubrid to fix its billing practices, address usability issues, and be more upfront about who’s hardware they’re selling to customers.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Radiant/Ori earns a ClusterMAX Unavailable rating from SemiAnalysis (introduced April 2026 in the ClusterMAX 2.1 Update).

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Radiant was announced recently after Brookfield acquired Ori, a Saudi Aramco backed neocloud with H100s and H200s in London and Dallas.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: When we tested with Ori on two occasions in the fall, we saw some quick progress but not enough to get to silver.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Ori fell victim to the exact same issues as FPT, with PKey and SAKey not configured correctly.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: In addition, during our first round of testing, we were unable to run nccl-tests at full bandwidth on kubernetes due to an issue with the NetworkOperator picking up NICs that were intended to be for the frontend but were named/configured incorrectly to be used for NCCL.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Finally, DCGMI health watches are not enabled by default, and there is no automated background health check program.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Our testing of a simple hardware failure simulation showed that the system did not trigger any automated alerting or node replacement over an 18-hour window.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: The team is targeting Q2 2026 for the release of monitoring dashboards, and seems well on their way to having the funding they need to build Blackwell clusters with comprehensive slurm, kubernetes, monitoring and reliability features customers expect.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Runpod earns a ClusterMAX 2.0 Bronze rating from SemiAnalysis.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Runpod manages a significant fleet of over 20,000 GPUs, with users all over the world.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: However, their fundamental architectural choice to put every user inside a “pod” (container) severely limits their ability to service large scale training, inference, and any enterprise workloads.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: In our testing, the container-centric design prevents the use of standard HPC and MLOps tools, such as running Slurm with Pyxis or Enroot for containerized MPI jobs, performing active health checks on the underlying bare-metal infrastructure, or using Kubernetes.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: In our testing of Runpod’s Slurm offering (still in Beta), we initially used a cluster directly from another provider, FarmGPU, and gave feedback on a number of issues we found.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: The Runpod technical team was responsive, took the feedback, and committed to actively incorporate this feedback in their next development cycle.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: A few weeks later, different Runpod team members insisted that we re-test with a different bare metal provider, directly from their console.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: While we appreciate their engagement, all the core issues we found on the first round of testing remained.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: The default user is root, with no way to add additional users, enforce RBAC, or use an external IAM provider.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: The default home directory (~) is not on a shared filesystem, forcing users to navigate to a separate /workspace directory.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: More critically, the environment lacks essential tooling. We found no pre-installed MPI, and initial attempts to run MPI-based jobs using srun failed due to a required hostfile modification, specifying external container hostnames and routes, since these are not updated in DNS or standard IPs.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Specifically, we had to export NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME=”ens1” because it was not pre-populated in /etc/nccl.conf, export HF_HOME=/workspace/.cache/huggingface because /root is the default workdir, not /workspace

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Even with knowledge of these custom approaches going into the second round of testing, it is currently still poorly documented and clearly a beta feature.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: On monitoring and health checks, we expect it will continue to be difficult for Runpod to ensure the reliability and performance required for large scale training.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: We have heard from multiple Runpod customers that since Runpod does not explicitly state which underlying hardware provider you’re going to land on (aside from specifying a “region”, and a binary “secure” or “community” cloud) that they effectively feel like they’re spinning a roulette wheel to try and “get a good pod”.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: In other words, users waste a bunch of time spinning up/down pods based on their perception of quality, because price-per-value information is not available to them in the console.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Overall, we expect Runpod will continue to serve a niche market that values its simplified, container-first approach, but it will struggle to make progress against our criteria without a fundamental change to their architecture.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Inference, and Kubernetes in general is not a significant part of their go-forward strategy.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: A significant recent improvement is the deployment of a “copilot” Grafana instance, which includes essential DCGM and slurm exporters.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: This directly addresses a criticism we made in the first version of this article, regarding a lack of monitoring in their offering.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Furthermore, Scaleway has enhanced reliability by implementing health checks through slurm prolog and epilog scripts, with monitoring data being actively managed to ensure cluster stability.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Interestingly, during testing, Scaleway worked with a customer to develop a synthetic benchmark better than nccl-tests, which indicated a 20% performance improvement over InfiniBand.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: However, in a crucial real-world test case, that performance advantage was not realized.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Looking ahead, Scaleway is still in the planning phase for Blackwell, and is targeting HGX B200/B300 baseboards only, rather than the fully integrated GB200 NVL systems.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: The company is also exploring AMD GPUs, but have yet to see significant customer traction in Europe.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Overall, Scaleway’s business model has begun to reflect a “European premium” for sovereign, GDPR-compliant infrastructure.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: This is evident in their resource allocation, which requires customers to contract for an entire cluster for large-scale jobs, rather than allowing on-demand access to single 8-way GPU machines.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: This model targets well-funded, serious AI projects, including an ecosystem built around the Scaleway Startup Program.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: This program offers credits and support, aiming to onboard the next generation of European tech companies.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: We expect Scaleway to continue to operate in a solid niche, prioritizing dedicated, high-performance clusters for, the European market with an associated premium.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Sesterce earns a ClusterMAX 2.0 Underperforming rating from SemiAnalysis.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Sesterce is a French cloud headquartered in Marseille, currently claiming access to 1GW of compute, 100k GPUs under management, and €750 million of investment.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: They started as a crypto miner, but have recently announced a Europe-sovereign €52 billion investment plan across multiple datacenters.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: This plan involves an initial site in Valence Romans Agglo, which will have 40k GPUs, totaling €1.8 billion.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: They then plan to add two additional sites in Grand Est, totalling 600 MW of capacity and 500,000 GPUs by 2028, with additional scaling to 1.2 GW and over 1 million GPUs by 2030. Big plans.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Back to the present day, Sesterce seems to have reasonable availability of NVIDIA GPUs across their “regions” in Helsinki, Kansas City, Des Moines, Salt Lake City, Dulles, New York, Calgary, Toronto, Mumbai, Osaka, Australia, Frankfurt, Amsterdam, Warsaw, Iceland, Norway, and Sweden.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: From this size and scale, it seems clear that individual VMs are being deployed in datacenters run by other providers. Pricing also reflects a scenario where this is some middleman getting paid.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Users can easily create volumes in the Region where they are planning to launch a GPU machine, and re-use these volumes on additional machines in the future. Nice feature.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Users can also configure a specific docker image to pre-load in the machines cache.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Our 1x B200 VM spun up in the Helsinki Datacenter, and upon login we found that the machine belongs to DataCrunch (now called Verda, another ClusterMAX bronze provider)

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Clusters can be requested (but not spun up on-demand) 16 nodes at a time in Helsinki for B200, or 1-4 nodes at a time in Marseille for H100 or H200.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Unfortunately, these clusters are just bare metal machines with a shared storage option. Sesterce does not offer Slurm or Kubernetes orchestration, monitoring dashboards for the clusters, or health checks.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: It also seems that RBAC with authentication from external IAM providers is not available.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: The machine also had nvidia drivers docker pre-installed, with the nvidia container toolkit configured and on the latest version.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Download speeds were solid from this Helsinki location, posting some of the fastest times to install pytorch, download an ngc pytorch container, and download a model from huggingface.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Overall, our experience from Sesterce was solid.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: We expect that for certain users, paying the Sesterce premium for availability and a proper setup of an individual development machine offsets some of the headache that is experienced with other clouds.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: We encourage Sesterce to get into the game with on-demand slurm and kubernetes clusters given the solid foundation that exists from their public cloud services.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Most importantly, we encourage Sesterce to make it clear which provider is actually running the machine on their underlying platform, and to publicly communicate a third-party attestation of simple security audits and compliance, such as SOC2 Type I or ISO 27001 in order to move into the ClusterMAX ratings.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Shadeform earns a ClusterMAX 2.0 Bronze rating from SemiAnalysis.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Shadeform operates as a marketplace for GPU compute rather than a direct provider, owning no GPUs for themselves.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Unlike other marketplaces, Shadeform has a lean team and only $2 million in funding, and focuses strictly on their software and brokering deals.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Their platform offers a transparent view of available GPU instances, uniquely identifying the underlying provider for each machine, such as Verda (formerly Datacrunch), Lambda, Voltage Park, Hydra Host, Digital Ocean and Nebius.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: This transparency extends to surfacing compliance information like SOC2 Type II and HIPAA certifications.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: In fact, as of our testing, Shadeform is providing access to GPUs from 23 different providers, the most we have seen on any marketplace.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Interestingly, Shadeform’s primary business has transformed, with them now entering into the wholesale bare-metal market as a broker.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: This means that a significant portion of their revenue comes via the negotiation and structuring of large-scale cluster deployments for their clients, particularly in the Asia-Pacific region (Taiwan, Japan, India).

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: The Shadeform website has become a valuable discovery tool for this purpose, and is often the first place neoclouds have their GPUs appear publicly.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Shadeform also appears to be the only partner currently in place for NVIDIA’s Brev offering, which we describe later in this article.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: With all that said, without a comprehensive Slurm or Kubernetes offering that we can test, no monitoring dashboards, and no way to do active/passive health checks on the underlying provider’s machines, we think it will be difficult for Shadeform to move beyond the bronze category.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: We look forward to testing cluster products and finding ways to evaluate the brokering services in the future.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: STN earns a ClusterMAX 2.0 Bronze rating from SemiAnalysis.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: STN is second in our list of providers that should be in the silver tier if our testing went better.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: By comparison, STN is similar to Cirrascale, which is to say STN offers dedicated managed services for clusters that are built-to-order for individual customers.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: There is no “public” cloud experience, and frankly not much about this is “cloud”. But customers who want a high-touch experience can get it here.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: In our testing, the STN platform is undermined by significant configuration errors and reliability problems, landing STN in our Bronze tier.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Onboarding is entirely manual, requiring phone calls to review PDFs and set up accounts.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: We were given a 4-node B200 cluster with impressive hardware, including four network fabrics (RoCEv2 for interconnect and storage) and 25TB of VAST.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: However, this high-end hardware was let down by basic configuration mistakes. For example, we found seven local NVMe drives unmounted on each node.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: The Slurm environment was also missing key components for performance: no topology.conf, GPUDirect RDMA was disabled (nvidia_peermem not loaded), and MPI was not installed.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Unfortunately, STN’s biggest weakness was reliability. During testing, we saw two different nodes go into a “down” state, one of which stayed “down” for over two days.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Since the STN repair process is entirely manual, it requires customers to spot and report failures themselves.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Notably, dcgm health -c is enabled on the nodes, but it is not plugged into Slurm as a HealthCheckProgram.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: We suggest that in the future, STN focus on actual cluster reliability instead of reporting fake “Uptime SLA” metrics to Grafana.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: It took weeks for STN engineers to modify the cluster to include hpcx, nccl, and nvcc, enable GPUDirectRDMA and turn off ACS so that we could a basic nccl-test and torchtitan training job to run on four nodes.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: We also ran into what looked like network traffic shaping over the WAN that slowed down our downloads, but made speedtest-cli look great.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: With all this said, in our conversations with customers, STN has demonstrated that they have the capability to do deep, custom work for their customers.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Going forward we suggest that STN work to automate a lot of its Slurm provisioning, health checks, and develop a comprehensive monitoring dashboard to improve reliability.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Until then, we feel that STN remains a high-risk choice and a Bronze-tier provider.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)

quote: A major Norwegian telco that has announced Norway’s first “AI Factory” in partnership with NVIDIA.

quote: The platform is not yet launched and is unavailable for testing, despite initial announcements being made back in February 2025.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Norway has one of the largest sovereign wealth funds in the world, a cool climate, and cheap green energy.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: We are excited to see what Telenor comes to market with in the future.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: TELUS earns a ClusterMAX 2.0 Unavailable rating from SemiAnalysis.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: TELUS is a major Canadian telco that has deployed GPUs in datacenters but is still “launching soon” with its own Sovereign play.
