speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Tensorwave earns a ClusterMAX 2.0 Silver rating from SemiAnalysis.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Tensorwave is a provider that recently raised a $100M Series A from AMD Ventures.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: As a result, they have an exclusive focus on AMD hardware, including 8,192 MI325X GPUs in their Tucson, Arizona datacenter.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Since we love all GPUs and love AMD, we have been working with Tensorwave for a long time as they graciously provide us access to GPUs for benchmarking that is well beyond the scope of ClusterMAX. We are grateful for this support.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Our testing on Tensorwave’s SonK platform has shown it to be largely unstable.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: The onboarding process is confusing, relying on Rancher’s RKE2 open-source kubernetes distribution (formerly RKE government), Longhorn for storage, and a modified version of Slinky for SonK (to get it to support AMD GPUs properly).

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: To login to the cluster we initially had to escalate to sudo just to run basic kubectl commands and get a “slurm-login” convenience script working.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: It took a significant amount of back and forth with the Tensorwave team to get a working kubeconfig (notably, this is now easy to download from the console).

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: We also ran into issues with permissions and user groups, which did not seem to be properly synchronized between the jump box and the Slurm login nodes.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: This issue has also been fixed since our testing period, but it is clear that there is limited experience getting an RBAC-scoped cluster working with an external IAM provider.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: In addition, the Slurm login node was missing the (now classic) tools we expect: vim, nano, git and sudo permissions to run apt install.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: However, in Tensorwave’s case, it only took a few hours for the team to modify the base container image to include these tools. We were impressed by this turnaround time.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: In addition to access, there was no topology-aware scheduling in place, health checks were not integrated with Slurm for auto-draining nodes that fail a health check, and the monitoring dashboard was missing critical information about GPU and system health that is unique to AMD’s

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: While NVIDIA providers get a simpler foundation building on DCGM, Tensorwave has had to build a lot of this from scratch, since they are AMD exclusive.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: During our testing, we have experienced a number of reliability issues, including some outages that stretch over multiple hours or days.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: In a two-month period, we have experienced 7 distinct interruptions: hardware and firmware issues on GPU nodes, a redeployment of Kubernetes, SonK/slurm-login connection issues, maintenance on Weka storage, maintenance on switches and routers, and even a power outage.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Notably, none of these issues are directly related to AMD GPUs, it is the rest of the cluster and the facilities around the GPU.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: To their credit, the Tensorwave team is always very responsive to our feedback and quick to address issues we raise. We have also seen a general trend of reliability improving over time.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Overall, the fact that we have to provide guidance on proper Slurm setup, monitoring, and health checks points to a general lack of experience running multi-tenant clusters at the scale of 8,192 MI325X GPUs or larger.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: We look forward to collaborating more with Tensorwave over time as they build out more AMD GPU capacity.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Together earns a ClusterMAX 2.0 Silver rating from SemiAnalysis.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Adequate offering with noticeable gaps compared to Gold or Platinum. Room for improvement.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Together is a strong provider with a robust cluster offering for both slurm and kubernetes, but it is held back from the gold category due to reliability issues.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: When comparing offers, we hear from users that they generally expect a lower price per GPU-hr from Together to justify the trade-off in reliability.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Together is among a few providers for which we tend to hear the most reliability complaints about from users operating clusters of 64 GPUs or more.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: We expect this is due to their use of a broad mix of datacenter partners, which creates a “roll-of-the-dice” dynamic for performance and stability.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Unfortunately, Together also does not offer to do 1-week POCs with most customers, unlike other Silver, Gold, and Platinum tier providers, which makes it difficult for buyers to know what sort of experience they will have on the cluster before making a multi-million dollar commitment.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: These are all the reasons why TogetherAI went from an Gold tier provider to Silver tier provider.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Together’s multi-datacenter strategy seems to be driven by necessity.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: They have significant compute needs due to their serverless inference endpoint business, which is growing steadily.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: During our research for this article, we spoke with multiple Neoclouds that claim Together is one of their biggest customers.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Competing in the serverless inference endpoint business does provide two key benefits: it creates a sales funnel to cross-sell GPU clusters to inference customers, and it allows Together to absorb the cost of idle cluster compute by running inference workloads on it.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: TKC is an exceptional feature, and the impact of Tri Dao’s FlashAttention cannot be overstated.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: During the research for this article, we got to hear directly from Dan Fu about the TKC roadmap.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: We suspect that Dan is the only person in the industry with the title of “VP, Kernels”, and for good reason.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: TKC is consistently impressive, and it helps both customers and Together’s serverless inference endpoint business achieve improved performance and efficiency.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Together’s model of offsetting costs from idle compute by running public and private serverless endpoints is now being copied by the likes of Nebius.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: During testing, we got access to a classic Together slurm cluster, a TKE kubernetes cluster, and a soon-to-be-released Instant Cluster in preview.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: For slurm, the onboarding process was smooth.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Just create an account on the console, upload ssh keys, and the together engineering team sends you an onboarding document.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: One ssh command and the cluster works out of the box.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Unfortunately, during testing we noticed that the cluster responded very slowly to terminal commands in a VSCode or cursor remote SSH session.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: The standard terminal application was fine, and we could replicate the slowness from multiple locations, leading us to believe it was a problem with their datacenter provider

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: The Kubernetes onboarding experience was less polished.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Instead of providing a kubeconfig file to download, we were expected to login and access the cluster via ssh.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: In addition, we found that standard tools like Helm were not installed, and users do not get sudo permissions by default, requiring more manual setup.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Together uses rancher k3s to provide these clusters, which is strange considering how much of the serverless endpoint runs on kubernetes.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Together has several customers, including Hedra, Cartesia, and Krea, that are successfully running production inference on thousands of GPUs using these managed K8s clusters.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: However, at this time, together does not have horizontal node autoscaling capabilities in these clusters.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Whatever capacity you commit to is what you get.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: “Instant Clusters” is Together’s newest offering, designed to be fully managed via API, CLI, and a Terraform provider.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: This product allows users to dynamically provision clusters and add or remove nodes on demand, making it suitable for handling burst capacity and autoscaling.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: The architecture for Instant Clusters provides strong tenant isolation using a multi-layered approach similar to Nebius.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: First, a base Kubernetes cluster uses KubeVirt to create dedicated Virtual Machines (VMs) for a customer.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Second, these VMs are used to form an isolated Kubernetes cluster dedicated to that customer.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Third, slurm is then installed into the customer’s dedicated K8s cluster using slurm-operator from Slinky.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Notably, in our testing, Together is the only provider to correctly configure Slinky out-of-the-box with sudo permissions, vim/nano, git, python, and other basic packages pre-installed.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: They clearly have already rolled out this offering to users, and we are excited for it to launch in full GA.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: On these clusters, Together provides 24/7 support from an on-call SRE team that is primarily US-based.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: For networking, they work directly with customers to configure firewall rules at the datacenter level and provide IP addresses as needed, including 1:1 NAT and public IPs assignable through services like MetalLB.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: The final, and most important piece of differentiation from Together and gold tier providers is a proactive and automated approach to monitoring and reliability.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: This has been a weak point for Together, and is difficult for them to work around given the broad use of datacenter and GPU infrastructure partners they have contracts with.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: During our review of the monitoring dashboard, we noted a bug in their Grafana monitoring dashboard that incorrectly reported InfiniBand bandwidth at a physically impossible 1.14 Tbit/s.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: To their credit, when we pointed this out, their team quickly identified the calculation error in their query and deployed a fix.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: For passive health checks, we expect checks run continuously in the background to detect failures on live nodes.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: This is where the gap between their current implementation and a fully automated system is most clear.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Together has implemented detection for many critical issues, including GPUs falling off the bus, PCIe errors, InfiniBand link flaps, high GPU thermals, and high ECC memory error rates.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: A baseline Kubernetes node health check is also in place.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: However, the most critical missing piece is automated remediation.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: While they can detect most of the issues above, the logic to automatically drain a faulty node is still on the roadmap for everything except for GPUs falling off the bus in slurm.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Other crucial features on the roadmap include detecting uncorrectable Nvidia XID errors, identifying stalled NCCL jobs, and implementing AI/ML-based predictive failure analysis.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: For active health checks, Together has currently implemented a comprehensive suite of tests for single-node validation.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: It includes Nvidia’s DCGM diagnostics (level 3), PCIe bandwidth tests, single-node NCCL and InfiniBand all-reduce tests to validate local interconnects, and GPU stress tests like GPUBurn.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: However, key multi-node and application-level tests are still on the roadmap.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: This includes pairwise ib_write tests to validate the InfiniBand fabric under load, hardware correctness validation with Nvidia’s TinyMeg2, and full-stack performance tests with models like Megatron to ensure TFLOPs and loss convergence match reference numbers.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: We encourage Together to prioritize implementing these active health checks, as we believe it will help them improve reliability, especially when working with datacenter partners that are not under their direct control.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: In summary, Together continues to operate on a solid foundation for managed clusters.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: They have a large and growing customer base for both their clusters, and serverless inference endpoint products.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Their active, single-node health checks are strong.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: However, the system is not yet complete.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: We believe that the gap between detecting node failures passively, instead of automatically remediating them proactively is a key reason for the reliability issues users experience today.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Vast.ai earns a ClusterMAX 2.0 Bronze rating from SemiAnalysis.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Vast.ai (not to be confused with Vast Data, the storage provider) operates as a GPU marketplace, not a direct provider.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: The platform claims SOC2 compliance is in place directly, and some other notable security information

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: They also state that many underlying datacenter providers are ISO27001 compliant, a notable step up from an aggregator, but still less introspection on who the underlying provider is than we would like since generally only the location is described.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Vast does provide ways for users to track datacenters by IDs, and toggle for a “secure cloud”, but does not expose who the underlying provider actually is outside of the country.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Clusters are available on a per-request basis and we have not been able to try one out.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Users can pay for their GPUs with stripe (credit card), coinbase, or crypto.com.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Our testing experience confirms the platform’s architectural focus: it is almost exclusively designed for containerized workloads, heavily pushing users toward Jupyter notebook environments.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Gaining basic SSH access required manual configuration steps, and once connected, it was clear we were operating inside a container, not a VM or bare-metal host.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: This container-only model immediately precludes standard multi-node orchestration like Slurm or native Kubernetes, though cluster-on-demand requests are available.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Reliability and performance are unpredictable, which is characteristic of the aggregator model.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Our first test instance was provisioned in Czechia, hosted by an unknown underlying provider (though an IP lookup suggests E-Infra or Zoner Cloud).

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: While this instance was functional, the marketplace model means users are rolling the dice on many qualities with every deployment.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Without the ability to test managed Slurm/Kubernetes, multi-node clusters, or review monitoring and health checks, Vast.ai remains a platform primarily built for individual developers and hobbyists.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Verda/DataCrunch earns a ClusterMAX 2.0 Bronze rating from SemiAnalysis.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Meets minimum criteria. Last category we directly recommend; often with inconsistent support or networking gaps.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Verda (formerly DataCrunch) is based in Finland, with datacenters in both Finland and Iceland.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: When logging in, Verda provides a nice clean console, making provisioning quite straightforward.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Their “Instant Clusters” feature was easy to use and spun up a slurm cluster in minutes.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: We were also impressed by the completeness of their Slurm implementation, which stands in stark contrast to many other providers on the bronze or even silver tier of this list.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: From this experience, it seems like they have battle-tested the offering with customers, despite it still being labelled as “Beta”.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Specifically, the B200 cluster we got had everything we expected: pyxis, enroot, hpcx, nccl, nvcc, topology.conf, dcgmi health -c plugged into Slurm’s HealthCheckProgram.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: On monitoring, the Grafana dashboard included an interesting SSH command to retrieve the password, and was relatively well configured.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Missing pieces related to job performance were minor, and we gave feedback how to make some improvements beyond standard DCGM metrics, and display them in a meaningful way to users.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: The platform also still lacks any way to add users with RBAC enforced at the storage or slurm level.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Overall, with working B200 instances available, and comprehensive slurm install, our initial impression was that Verda had made significant improvements from our last round of testing.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: However, this solid software foundation is still undermined by significant issues on the business and operations side.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: We have heard about reliability issues from various Verda customers, both at the hardware level and with respect to their WAN connectivity.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Specifically, Verda customers have told us that entire sites can go dark with no explanation.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Unfortunately, we have seen Verda charge their customers for GPU time even when instances are down or entire sites are inaccessible.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: To us, this is an offensive business practice.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Our basic expectation for all cloud providers is to commit to their SLAs in written form, with penalties in the form of credits or deductions off a customer’s monthly bill in the event of a breach.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Not upholding a written SLA undermines many of the technical benefits and attractive pricing that we have seen from Verda during our testing.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Note: since publishing this article we’ve discussed this issue in detail with Verda.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Verda is committed to compensate any customers who experience downtime with at least 2x the cost of running any instances in the form of a credit.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Customers contacting technical support via chat get an automatic message stating that all downtime will be compensated.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Verda typically issues refunds within 24 hours of the downtime occurrence during weekdays, and on the following Monday for downtimes occurring during weekends.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: For customers billed monthly, any downtime or defects are compensated by subtracting the corresponding amount from the monthly invoice.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Frankly, we think this is an excellent response.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: In general, SemiAnalysis recommends that customers be sure to keep server logs, screenshots, and other information readily available if they are pursuing downtime claims from their provider.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: At this time we have only seen gold or platinum tier providers proactively issue credits without customers asking for them.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Overall we recommend that Verda shore up their reliability challenges, finalize their slurm offering currently in beta, improve the monitoring dashboard, and continue development of their kubernetes offering.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: We look forward to seeing more from Verda in the future.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Voltage Park earns a ClusterMAX 2.0 Silver rating from SemiAnalysis.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Adequate offering with noticeable gaps compared to Gold or Platinum. Room for improvement.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Voltage Park is a story of turnaround and redemption.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: If we were to have done this review in 2023 or 2024, the story would have been much different.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: The current Voltage Park is who we are rating, and the current Voltage Park is a reasonably less weak provider focused exclusively on H100 GPUs.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: As of our testing, their on-demand capacity appears to be regularly sold out.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: The company is shipping features at a rapid pace, including a recently launched SLURM service and OIDC integration for Kubernetes.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Voltage park offers the one of the lowest price in the industry.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Our initial experience with slurm included a lot of provisioning challenges, with multiple attempts being required to spin up our test cluster.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Once provisioned, we would be load balanced to different login nodes, with the now-classic SonK issue of not being able to run code.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Not git, vim, nano, or sudo permissions.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: However, Voltage Park is the only provider with these SonK issues that seemed to be aware of them, suggesting a kubectl exec command to access the login pod, instead of the original ssh via public IP.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: While this container-first approach got us to workaround the initial root permission issue, it still takes time to install software, and if your connection gets reset, all software installs go away.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: In other words, login pods are stateless.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: The Voltage Park engineering team committed to building a new container image for login pods that included necessary software to run slurm jobs and edit code, and they delivered just that in under 24 hours.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: We were impressed by the commitment to customer support.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: We found a correctly configured topology.conf for network-aware scheduling, SLURM prolog and epilog scripts in place, and a modern container toolkit with pyxis and enroot installed.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Interconnect performance was strong, running collectives at expected bandwidth.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: We also saw good download speeds, and a reasonably fast shared filesystem.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Operationally, we encountered two major points of concern.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: First, Voltage Park’s dashboard has a “Shutdown” function that is distinct from “Terminate”.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: “Shutdown” halts the instances but continues to bill for the reserved capacity, a nuance that is not made sufficiently clear in the UI, and we expect is a disaster waiting to happen.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Notably, not a single other provider offers these distinct “Shutdown” and “Terminate” options, and even after discussing the purpose of the “Shutdown” button with the Voltage Park team, it is still very confusing to us what the intended use case is.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Second, their process for handling hardware failures in on-demand clusters is manual, requiring operator intervention to cycle nodes out of a user’s cluster.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: This is a far cry from the automated, resilient systems offered by top-tier providers.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: This is also demonstrated by a lack of up-to-date security patches.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: The cluster was also pre-installed with an nvidia container toolkit version (1.17.4) that was out-of-date by 9 months, and as discussed previously in this article, victim to CVE-2025-23266 (NVIDIAScape) and CVE-2025-23267, with CVSS scores of 9.0 and 8.5 out of 10 respectively (“Critical”).

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: In conclusion, we believe that Voltage Park now has a solid technical foundation to carry forward and recover from reputational issues.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: We are encouraged by the execution of the technical team, and look forward to seeing more improvements in the future.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Vultr earns a ClusterMAX 2.0 Silver rating from SemiAnalysis.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: To kick things off, Vultr set the record for this round of ClusterMAX by bringing 12 people onto our kickoff call.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Vultr raised money last year at a $3.5B valuation, including an investment from AMD Ventures, and this past summer also got $329M of debt financing.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: As a result, Vultr now offers AMD MI355X GPUs (backstopped by AMD) and an expanding fleet of NVIDIA GPUs (including HGX B200), across some of their 32 global regions.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: When we started our testing, the Vultr SLURM service seemed brand new, like a second class citizen in the console.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: The cluster was missing pyxis, hpcx, topology.conf, the default login user was “root” (with no default workdir).

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Most importantly, there was no shared home filesystem.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: We recommended some basic fixes, and quickly got going with an “ubuntu” user, with a default workdir switched to a shared /mnt/vfs.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Eventually, we were able to get nccl-tests at expected bandwidth, and some basic torchtitan training runs going at expected MFU.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: When we were handed our kuberenetes cluster, we unfortunately got versions of the NVIDIA GPU Operator and Network Operator that were over 1 year old, meaning they were subject to three separate “critical” level CVEs, such as NVIDIAscape from Wiz

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: We recommended an upgrade, and the team mentioned they were “writing the jira for it”.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: During testing, we had some intermittent link flaps that eventually went away on their own.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Unfortunately, there was no proactive notification or remediation of this, due to a lack of a monitoring dashboard and any active or passive health checks on the cluster’s interconnect.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: One of the team members, Enis, was familiar enough with KubeFlow to get it installed and configure an example torchtitan training job to work on their network. We were impressed!

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: After shifting to inference, we saw a strong showing from VKE.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: The Vultr Cloud Controller Manager runs as part of Vultr’s managed control plane (not visible in the cluster), and handles automatic provisioning of resources like a LoadBalancer public IP.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Reasonable default helm charts were installed, and it was easy to configure new ones, thanks to a default ReadWriteMany StorageClass being configured.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Following our feedback, Vultr has joined the NVIDIA embargo program to ensure they are notified ahead of time for future security vulnerabilities.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Vultr’s outreach to AMD’s Product Security Office seems to have motivated AMD to develop a similar security embargo program on their own.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: We appreciate Vultr’s commitment to improvement and the direct engagement from their engineers.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: We recommend that they work on developing a monitoring dashboard, active and passive health checks, and continue building experience operating large GPU clusters.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Whitefiber earns a ClusterMAX 2.0 Underperforming rating from SemiAnalysis.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Whitefiber is a wholly-owned subsidiary of Bit Digital, another company which has recently pivoted from crypto mining to Ethereum staking and AI.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Whitefiber went public on the NASDAQ in August 2025, raising approximately $150M.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: The combined company ($WYFI and $BTBT) has a market cap approaching $1B.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Bit Digital recently announced a North Carolina datacenter that can expand from 24MW to 99MW, a large augmentation to their existing footprint in Montreal, with the intention to host more AI customers.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: In the past the company has mentioned LOI’s for 288MW, and they have publicly announced contracts for 4,096 H100, 1,040 H200, and 464 B200.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: In our testing, Whitefiber’s networking was within the reference numbers if not slightly better for some message sizes.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: In terms of other aspects, we were sadly disappointed and did not match the same quality as their networking.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: we were given a Slinky cluster, with access to both the slurm and kubernetes layer. Unfortunately, neither of them worked.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Initially, slurm was inaccessible from a remote machine, with lots of negotiation required to make it work.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Meanwhile, at the kubernetes layer, nothing could be scheduled since slurm-bridge was not configured, and all GPU resources were taken by slinky.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Eventually, we got a jump box working to get into the slurm cluster, and found the typical slinky footguns: no git, vim, nano, python, or sudo permissions to install software.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Cluster dashboards were long and detailed but missing important metrics about jobs.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: No active or passive health checks could be found.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: We were given access to dashboards for clockwork and trainy, neither of which were explained or documented, and were therefore not useful in our testing.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Whitefiber has clearly made investments in their AI cloud offering by hiring a large team of consultants, integrating a custom interconnect to replace NVIDIA, and buying every piece of software pitched to them.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Unfortunately, they are held back even from the bronze category for lacking a basic security attestation from a third party auditor, such as SOC 2 Type I/II or ISO27001.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: We believe that by ClusterMAX 2.1 or ClusterMAX 3 if Whitefiber gets a basic SOC2 Type I compliance in place and fixes their SLURM/Kubernetes orchestration, they would find themselves in at least the bronze tier.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Yotta earns a ClusterMAX 2.0 Unavailable rating from SemiAnalysis.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Yotta’s Shakti Cloud (not to be confused with the datacenter industry conference “Yotta”, going by the same name) was the first mover in India’s sovereign AI push, and according to Jensen his “favourite cloud in Asia”.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: Yotta has announced over 16,000 H100 GPUs are deployed in Shakti, with Blackwell currently being deployed and more on the way.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: This maintains Yotta’s status with the most GPUs in India at 32,768 total by end of 2025.

speaker: Jordan Nanos, Daniel Nishball, Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)
quote: We regret the difficulties experienced so far in testing Yotta’s cloud services and look forward to including them for testing in ClusterMAX 2.1 coming soon.
